messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary failure rate exceeded threshold for rollout 'payment-checkout-canary' — variant=redwood-7b-q3, region=us-west1, fail_rate=12.7% :rotating_light:
oncall-jay: picking this up. assigning self. Paging SRE.
alex: seeing spike in 5xx and latency tail to 800ms in us-west1, looks correlated with canary traffic. logs show mismatch in model variant hash vs routing table.
maria: can you paste the metric and a quick top-5 errors?
alex: top errors: 
```
ERROR model-mismatch: expected variant 'redwood-7b-q3' got 'redwood-7b-q2-compat'
ERROR kv-cache-miss: eviction storm on 3 pods
```
kira: that suggests fallback routing is sticky to the wrong variant after the canary started failing. sticky TTL is 30m currently. if users hit canary and it fails, sticky fallback pins them to fallback variant even after it recovers.
oncall-jay: can we confirm fallback policy? show me routing config snapshot from config-store.
infra-jen: pulled config at 2539990000: 
```yaml
routing_policies:
  payment-checkout-canary:
    traffic_split: 5%->redwood-7b-q3, 95%->redwood-7b-q2-compat
    fallback: sticky
    sticky_ttl: 1800 # seconds
```
oncall-jay: that's the culprit. sticky fallback + TTL too long + canary failures = sustained stuck sessions. need mitigation fast.
sre-bot: suggested actions: 1) pause canary rollout 2) evict sticky affinities for payment-checkout route 3) reduce sticky_ttl temporarily to 60s 4) monitor customer impact
alex: starting with pause in console now. 
product-sylvia: heads-up — two enterprise customers (acme-pay, bluecart) reported errors; support already alerted them.
support-raj: acme-pay reported checkout failures for a subset of users (approx 2% of their calls) starting ~10:12 UTC. we offered workaround (force-retry) and collecting logs.
oncall-jay: pausing canary -> command: 
```bash
redwoodctl rollout pause --route payment-checkout-canary --by oncall-jay
```
jen: paused, confirmed. traffic split reverted to stable 100%->redwood-7b-q2-compat.
maria: next, we need to clear sticky affinities from the routing cache. run: 
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routes/payment-checkout/evict-affinities
```
alex: evict job kicked off, hitting 200 responses from control-plane. will take ~30s to propagate.
kira: also set sticky_ttl to 60s so newly created fallbacks don't stick long.
oncall-jay: apply config patch: 
```yaml
patch:
  routing_policies:
    payment-checkout-canary:
      sticky_ttl: 60
      fallback: round_robin
```
infra-jen: pushed patch via config-store, reloaded routing layer. confirmed policy now fallback=round_robin & sticky_ttl=60.
sre-bot: monitoring signals: canary errors dropping, 5xx back to baseline in us-west1.
alex: post-eviction rate check: fail_rate now 0.9% at 2539991500, latency p95 down to 160ms.
product-sylvia: please flag impacted customers for outreach, escalate if any SLA breaches.
support-raj: sending consolidated incident note to acme-pay and bluecart now.
oncall-jay: good. keep this thread for handoff. I'm escalating to incident review for postmortem. assigning postmortem owner: kira.
kira: taking PM for postmortem. will collect timeline, root cause: sticky fallback policy + TTL + canary variant mismatch + config rollback gap.
alex: also adding immediate action item: gating sticky fallback for canaries unless explicit opt-in.
infra-jen: filing infra task to add a control in console + API to force affinity eviction on rollout state changes.
product-sylvia: add customer-impact section to postmortem and include remediation timeline for SLA adjustments if needed.
sre-bot: incident severity set to SEV-2. page logs and metrics archived to: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2539990123/artifacts
oncall-jay: thanks all. I'll hand off to oncall weekly rotation — next oncall is kira, tagging for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
kira: acknowledged, I'll drive the postmortem and remediation PRs. closing live mitigation now; keeping thread open for a few hours for follow-ups.
support-raj: closing customer comms loop. thanks everyone. :pray:
